financing.summary: Toll Brothers is an investment-grade luxury builder (Moody's Baa2, S&P BBB, Fitch BBB+) that funds itself with cash flow, $1.75 billion of unsecured senior notes, a $650 million bank term loan and an undrawn $2.375 billion revolver; at July 31, 2026 it held $1.06 billion of cash and net debt to capital was 15.6%. It controls about 75,500 lots, of which about 58% are optioned rather than owned, mostly through land purchase contracts with sellers and developers ($8.16 billion aggregate purchase price, $872 million of deposits) and through 21 land development joint ventures. Its filings show it also uses third-party 'land bank programs' (cash-flow lines for sales to and repurchases from land bank programs appear from fiscal 2025), but the flows are small ($52 million of proceeds in fiscal 2025, $20 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026) and no land banker is named. Liabilities for consolidated inventory not owned have grown from $389 million (October 2024) to $857 million (July 2026), which shows growing use of structured, off-balance-sheet-style lot control. Room for a land banker exists but Toll is not capital-constrained: it has no notes due before March 2027, is buying back about $700 million of stock in fiscal 2026 and describes its direction as 'more asset-light'.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving toward land-light. Toll says it seeks option agreements to defer land purchases until closer to home delivery, and lists controlling land through options before taking title as a main way it improves capital efficiency; it also buys lots from land development joint ventures, which it calls more capital efficient but generally more expensive than outright purchases. No numeric optioned target is stated in the filings read; optioned share was about 55% at October 2024, 57% at October 2025 and 58% at July 2026.

lots.source_title: Toll Brothers FY2026 third quarter results press release (8-K exhibit 99.1)
lots.note: Release states about 75,500 lots owned and optioned, about 42% (31,800) owned; its home-sites table gives 31,817 owned and 43,669 optioned. About 18,100 owned lots were substantially improved. Years of supply is derived, not stated: total lots divided by fiscal 2026 delivery guidance midpoint (10,550 homes). Fiscal year-end comparison (10-K): about 76,100 lots at October 31, 2025, about 33,000 owned and 43,100 optioned. Q3 land spend was about $451.9 million for about 2,784 lots. Fiscal Q4 2026 results are due December 8, 2026.

land_banking.counterparty: Undisclosed land bank programs (land bankers not named in filings)
land_banking.description: Toll's cash flow statement carries two financing lines for land bank programs: proceeds from sales to land bank programs and payments for repurchases from them. Fiscal 2025: $52.1 million of proceeds and $91.5 million of repurchases. First nine months of fiscal 2026: $19.8 million of proceeds and $27.6 million of repurchases. The arrangements are treated as financings and the counterparties and program size are not disclosed.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: condensed consolidated statements of cash flows
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m is the nine-month fiscal 2026 proceeds figure. Fiscal 2025 figures are from the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/794170/000079417025000112/R7.htm), where both lines are zero for fiscal 2024 and 2023. The FY2025 10-K risk factors also say land financing may come indirectly through land banks or other land financing vehicles. No narrative description of the programs was found in the notes read.

land_banking.counterparty: Land sellers and developers under option / purchase contracts (not named)
land_banking.description: The bulk of Toll's optioned position is land purchase contracts. At July 31, 2026 the aggregate purchase price was $8.16 billion ($8.09 billion with unrelated parties, $76 million with unconsolidated entities) against $872.4 million of deposits; $847.7 million of the remaining cash required is already accrued. 326 of the contracts are with variable interest entities (aggregate price $7.53 billion, deposits $862.3 million); Toll is not the primary beneficiary of any.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: Commitments and Contingencies note (land purchase contracts)
land_banking.note: VIE contract figures are from the Inventory note of the same 10-Q (R9.htm). Accrued expenses include $856.9 million of 'liabilities related to consolidated inventory not owned' at July 31, 2026, up from $754.8 million at October 31, 2025 and $388.8 million at October 31, 2024 (10-Q R13.htm and FY2025 10-K R13.htm). The lots figure is total optioned lots from the Q3 release and includes lots optioned from joint ventures. Comparison: $7.54 billion aggregate price and $744.5 million deposits at October 31, 2025.

land_banking.counterparty: Toll's own land development joint ventures (partners not named)
land_banking.description: Toll sources finished lots from land development joint ventures it co-invests in. At July 31, 2026 it expected to buy about 8,600 more home sites from these ventures over several years at prices to be set later, on top of $76.1 million of contracted purchases from unconsolidated entities. It bought $117.4 million of land from unconsolidated entities in the first nine months of fiscal 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: land purchase contracts details
land_banking.note: FY2025 10-K: the land development JVs owned about 28,900 home sites at October 31, 2025, of which 832 were under contract to Toll; expected further purchases were then about 8,800 sites.

joint_ventures.partner: Land development joint ventures (21 entities; partners described only as other builders or financial partners)
joint_ventures.description: At July 31, 2026 Toll had $595.4 million invested in 21 land development JVs, with $265.1 million of remaining funding commitments to nine of them. Eighteen of the ventures carry debt: $1.12 billion of loan commitments, $695.2 million borrowed. One new land development JV was formed in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (five in the same period of fiscal 2025), and Toll sold its interest in one. Toll expects to buy about 8,600 home sites from these ventures.

ma.description: Toll bought substantially all the assets and operations of Buffington Homes of Arkansas, a private builder based in Fayetteville founded in 2010 and described as the largest luxury builder in northwest Arkansas. The deal brought nine active or coming-soon communities and about 1,500 home sites owned or controlled. Announced April 21, 2026; closed May 2026. Price not disclosed; accounted for as an asset acquisition and not material. Builder Advisor Group (Tony Avila) advised the seller.
ma.map_impact: Adds a new market (Fayetteville/Bentonville) and a new state, Arkansas. Founding partners Clay Carlton and Mike Lamberth stay on and focus on land acquisition and development, so they are the land contacts for northwest Arkansas; Buffington's senior leadership and employees joined Toll. Adds about 1,500 lots (about 2% of Toll's total); no change to Toll's rank. Buffington should be removed or marked as acquired if it appears as a separate builder.
ma.source_title: Toll Brothers to Acquire Private Home Builder in Northwest Arkansas (April 21, 2026)
ma.note: Closing month is from the Acquisition note of the July 31, 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/794170/000079417026000102/R8.htm); the exact closing day is not disclosed. after_ranking is set true because closing was in May 2026, although the announcement (April 21) came before the ranking was published. This is Toll's 16th builder acquisition since 1995 and its first since Rialto Homes in 2022.

ma.description: Toll announced its exit from multifamily development and agreed to sell the Toll Brothers Apartment Living platform, its interests in 18 apartment and student housing properties and a pipeline of 29 development sites to Kennedy Wilson. Most of the sale, including the platform, closed in December 2025 and the rest in the first half of fiscal 2026; nothing was held for sale at July 31, 2026. Toll received net cash of about $330 million and kept interests in 20 properties that it will sell over time.
ma.map_impact: Removes the Apartment Living business and its people from the Toll map: the Apartment Living executive team and development staff were expected to move to Kennedy Wilson. Frees about $330 million of capital for homebuilding land and buybacks. Apartment land contracts fell from $326.2 million to $13.8 million. No effect on homebuilding lots or rank.
ma.source_title: Kennedy Wilson and Toll Brothers joint press release (8-K exhibit, September 18, 2025)
ma.note: Price is stated differently by source: $347 million in the joint release, about $380 million as adjusted in Toll's FY2025 10-K, and about $330 million of net cash proceeds in the July 31, 2026 10-Q. Advisers to Toll: Goldman Sachs, Vestra Advisors, Fried Frank. Kennedy Wilson is not Kennedy Lewis.
